{{Quote|I can see why Narmle ''[sic]'' eventually gave up on colonizing this place. I haven't seen such an overgrown planet in a long time.''"<br />"''First off, remember that this is a moon, not a planet.|Dusque Mistflier and Tendau Nandon|<ref name="TRoD">''[[Star Wars Galaxies: The Ruins of Dantooine]]''</ref>}}
'''Rori''' was the second largest of three [[Moon/Legends|moons]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. Located in the [[Chommell sector/Legends|Chommell sector]] of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]], Rori was an overgrown, wild world dominated by oppressive [[Color/Legends|gray]] skies, thick [[Jungle/Legends|jungles]], and thick [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]]. The [[Forest/Legends|forests]] and other [[Plant/Legends|vegetation]] were said to be more twisted and knotted than Naboo's plantlife. Rori's early [[Historian/Legends|history]] was shrouded in mystery, but the moon was officially colonized during the [[Standard day/Legends|days]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] under the rule of [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|King]] [[Narmlé]], following the construction of [[Gender/Legends|his]] [[Narmle (city)|namesake]] [[City/Legends|city]]. During later [[Standard year/Legends|years]], a second city named [[Restuss]] was constructed to act as a quarantined processing center after an outbreak of [[Brainrot Plague|Brainworm Rot]]. Under [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Kylantha]]'s rule, following the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], Rori saw only limited involvement in the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] between the Empire and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. That all changed however, when by at least [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], the [[Battle of Restuss]] erupted, resulting in the complete devastation of one of Rori's only cities.

==History==
===Early colonization===
{{Quote|There's so much speculation about Naboo's moon in general, I don't know if anybody knows the straight answer."<br />"What do you mean?"<br />"Well, I'm no historian, but I don't think folks can even agree on who colonized Rori, let alone what is and isn't indigenous to the place. As I understand it, some say the original human colonists of Naboo landed there first, hated it because it was too inhospitable, and then came here. Others say that a group of spice miners went there first in search of the mother lode. Nobody can agree."<br />"Actually, I heard that it was Gungans who first built a settlement there."<br />"See what I mean? No one has the same story.|"Fingers" and her friend|<ref name="TRoD" />}}
[[File:Rori_Prima.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Another view of Rori]]
[[Millennium/Legends|Millennia]] before a group of [[Human/Legends|Humans]]<ref name="TEA" /> from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] of [[Grizmallt/Legends|Grizmallt]]<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> colonized [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]<ref name="TEA" /> around [[3900 BBY/Legends|3900 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> a mysterious [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] known as the [[Elders (Naboo)/Legends|"Elders"]]<ref name="FF59">{{FactFile|59|NAB 23-24|Naboo &ndash; Gungan Sacred Place}}</ref> established a presence on the [[Planet/Legends|world]].<ref name="AED" /> As proof of their visitations, the Elders left behind large stone colossi on both Naboo<ref name="FF59" /> and Rori. Otherwise, Rori's early [[Historian/Legends|history]] was somewhat contested by [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] [[Scholar/Legends|scholars]]. Some claimed that a small contingent of Naboo's original Human colonists actually landed on Rori before traveling on to the more temperate parent planet. If this was true, those early settlers left no obvious signs of their stay. Others held that Rori remained unsettled until a small group of [[Spice/Legends|spice]] [[Miner/Legends|miners]] decided to relocate to the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] in search of fabled spice lodes. Some spice miners did, in fact, inhabit Rori, but they lived a primitive lifestyle and had no records of their first landing on the moon.<ref name="AED" /> Others heard that the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] were the first to build a settlement there.<ref name="Ruins" /> Whatever the truth, Rori was officially colonized about two thousand [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]]<ref name="AED" /> around [[2032 BBY]],<ref name="TERC" /> during the short-lived reign of [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|King]] [[Narmlé]]. Although widely regarded as a charming and intelligent [[Gender/Legends|man]], Narmlé was a restless [[Scout/Legends|explorer]] who spent most of his [[Time/Legends|time]] visiting distant worlds in search of new vistas. The [[Naboo Royal Advisory Council/Legends|Naboo Royal Advisory Council]] soon suggested that Narmlé relinquish the [[Throne/Legends|throne]] and become an [[Ambassador/Legends|ambassador]]. Before leaving office as [[King/Legends|King]], however, Narmlé personally planned the construction of a small settlement on Rori named [[Narmle (city)|Narmle]]. He envisioned that Rori would one day become an active agricultural hub, supplying [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]] and medicines to other neighboring planets. Unfortunately for him, Rori attracted few settlers. Frustrated, Narmlé left Rori and vanished into the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] forever, although the [[City/Legends|city]] he helped build still bore his name.<ref name="AED" />

===Decline of the Republic===
{{Quote|Our intelligence points to disgruntled spice miners on the moons of Naboo.|Mace Windu, to Padmé Amidala|audio=AOTC-MoonsOfNaboo.flac|<ref name="AotC">{{Film|II}}</ref>}}
[[File:RoriFlag.png|150px|thumb|The flag of Rori]]
In the centuries since Narmlé's disappearance, Rori's population had grown only slightly. During an outbreak of [[Brainrot Plague|Brainworm Rot]] some two hundred years before the Battle of Naboo,<ref name="AED" /> around [[232 BBY/Legends|232 BBY]],<ref name="TERC" /> the Advisory Council commissioned the construction of a second [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] on Rori; this city, known as [[Restuss]], was used for decades as a quarantined processing center for colonists traveling to Naboo. [[Medic/Legends|Medical]] research conducted in Narmle eventually helped cure the [[Disease/Legends|plague]], and [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] officials rewarded the city for its efforts by funding the construction of a [[Center for Arts and Education]]. Although both Restuss and Narmle were built by Naboo [[Architect/Legends|architects]], most of the colonists during that time had been drawn from other, less hospitable worlds, including [[Iridonia/Legends|Iridonia]] and [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]]. The Gungans, who colonized the Naboo moon of [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]], had also established small outposts on Rori. One particular group of Gungans relocated to Rori shortly after the peace brokered between [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Rugor Nass]] and [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] as a result of the Battle of Naboo<ref name="AED" /> in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="TERC" /> These [[Rorgungans|Rorian Gungans]], who eventually operated out of a town known as the [[Gungan Swamp Town]], were violently opposed to any alliance between Humans and Gungans. Living in relative isolation, the Rorgungans had become territorial, paranoid, and increasingly violent to outsiders.<ref name="AED" /> In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="TEA" /> the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] suspected that disgruntled spice miners on the moons of Naboo were responsible for the [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala/Legends|plot]] to [[Assassin/Legends|assassinate]] Padmé Amidala.<ref name="AotC" />

===Rise of the Empire===
The [[Royal House of Naboo/Legends|Royal House of Naboo]] had typically viewed Rori as an extension of their domain. As a result, Rori received regular supplies from Naboo and travel between the moon and its parent planet was routine. Members of the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]] were stationed in both Restuss and Narmle, and Rori's [[Governor of Rori|governor]] sat on the Naboo Royal Advisory Council.<ref name="AED" /> During the rise of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]],<ref name="Apailana">{{CSWECite|I|37|Apailana, Queen}}</ref> [[Kylantha]]<ref name="AED" /> succeeded Queen [[Apailana/Legends|Apailana]] to the throne of Naboo<ref name="Apailana" /> in [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]],<ref name="Blog">{{Blog|holocron|22/comments|Movie Characters killed in the EU}}</ref> after the latter was [[Battle of Naboo (Imperial Period)|executed]] by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] for [[Treason/Legends|treason]].<ref name="Battlefront II">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref> Under their domain, the Empire viewed Rori as little more than a small Naboo outpost and expected all of the moon's inhabitants to remain loyal to [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]. In reality, Rori's denizens were far more independent than the "planetary" Naboo and it was believed that the moon harbored some members of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. Rori went largely unnoticed by most of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] as the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] intensified between the Galactic Empire and the Rebellion. [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Ferrox]] was charged with ruling the entire population of the moon, and had his home and offices in the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of Narmle. Narmle maintained a friendly rivalry with its sister city, Restuss. As the only cities on Rori, Narmle and Restuss typically competed for funds, visitors, and settlers from Naboo. Narmle's inhabitants often exhibited a sense of superiority, stemming from the fact that Narmle natives actually built Restuss. The rivalry had become heated on occasion, although it had only rarely erupted into violence.<ref name="AED" />

===Seeds of Rebellion===
By the time following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], the Rebel Alliance had established an outpost on Rori called [[Zephyr Base]]. The Rebels liaised with the Gungans, particularly [[Booto Lubble]], in planning operations against Imperial activity on Naboo. Besides Lubble, other Rebels operating from the base included [[Raxa Binn]], [[Vordin Sildor]], and [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[General/Legends|General]] [[Ufwol]], [[Commanding officer/Legends|commanding officer]] for the [[Crimson Phoenix Squadron]].<ref name="AED" /> After being forced to evacuate their [[Rebel Military Base (Tatooine)|military base]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], Rebel forces relocated to Rori to establish yet another [[Rebel Base (Rori)|base]]<ref name="Publish">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=64185&resource=publish|text=Publish Archive 2003}}</ref> northwest of [[Lake Octir]]. The Rebellion even contested the Empire's control of the [[Hyperdrive Research Facility]] elsewhere on Rori. Unfortunately for the Empire, the Rebels were not the only ones to oppose their rule on the moon. [[Vigo/Legends|Ex-vigos]] of [[Alexi Garyn]] managed, through luck and coincidence, to avoid [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul's]] destruction of the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] crime syndicate's leadership. They remained fiercely loyal to their leader,<ref name="AED" /> who was drowned by [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Maul in [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]].<ref name="DM4">[[Darth Maul (2000) 4|''Darth Maul'' (2000) 4]]</ref> After Alexi's [[Death/Legends|death]], his loyal followers had since banded together on Rori to harass Imperial [[Troop/Legends|troops]]. Known as the [[Garyn Raiders]], the resistance organization operated out of a [[Garyn Raider's Bunker|bunker]] and a [[Garyn Raider Base|small base]] on the swamp moon. Remnants of the [[Cobral family]], known as the [[Neo-Cobral]], also fled to Rori. Although they had lost much of their power and authority, rumor had it that a group of Cobral thieves had stolen some important documents from the Empire, and kept the information at their [[Cobral Hideout|hideout]]. Led by the [[Cobral Overlord]], the organization was bent on dominating the entire moon.<ref name="AED" />

In spite of this growing resistance, the Empire commanded a modest presence on the world, particularly in a large [[Imperial Encampment]] south of Narmle defended by [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|All Terrain Scout Transports]] and many [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] and [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officers]]. Specialized [[Stormtrooper sniper/Legends|stormtrooper snipers]] and [[Dark Trooper/Legends|dark troopers]] were also posted to this encampment. In Narmle, an Imperial [[Major/Legends|major]] attempted to trick members of the Rebellion to visit this base, under the pretense of peace negotiations. In fact, he had ordered the stormtroopers to shoot and kill any unauthorized visitors. Elsewhere on Rori, an Imperial [[Officer/Legends|officer]] named [[M'Kae/Legends|M'Kae]] staffed yet another [[Imperial Base (Rori)|base]] in a hilly region of Rori, alongside General [[Brant Korra]]. An Imperial [[Surface Marshal]] and [[Imperial Army trooper/Legends|Imperial Army troopers]] were also posted to at least one other small Rorian [[Imperial outpost (Rori)|outpost]].<ref name="AED" /> During [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> a Human [[Xenobiologist/Legends|xenobiologist]] of the [[Imperial Corps of Bioengineers/Legends|Imperial Corps of Bioengineers]] named [[Dusque Mistflier]], and her fellow [[Ithorian/Legends|Ithorian]] [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] [[Tendau Nandon]], visited the [[Aerie Casino]] on Naboo. During their stay, they overheard a [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] [[Beastmaster/Legends|creature handler]] nicknamed "[[Fingers]]" debate with her friend about the specifics of Rori's early history and indigenous life. Intrigued by what she overheard, Dusque implored Tendau to join her on an exploratory mission to Rori to study the world's fauna. Tendau reluctantly agreed to travel with Dusque, despite lacking the proper Imperial endorsements. During their time on Rori, the pair of xenobiologists stayed in Narmle, and took the time to explore an expansive [[Borgle Bat Cave|cave]] inhabited by [[borgle bat]]s.<ref name="Ruins" />

===The Battle of Restuss===
[[File:RoriElders.jpg|230px|thumb|The Elders' statues on Rori]]
{{Quote|I am Marles Jacobe of the Corellia Times. I am investigating the military buildup here in Restuss. It has already caused the entire city to be evacuated, displacing thousands of families. And with tensions running high there is sure to be a showdown. What are your thoughts on this whole situation?|[[Marles Jacobe]] to a [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]]|<ref name="SWG:SK">{{GalaxiesNGE}}</ref>}}
Perhaps, or rather because of its history, or the fact that Governor Ferrox rarely visited, Restuss seemed even further removed from Naboo [[Politics/Legends|politics]] than its sister city. It was not uncommon to meet a Restuss citizen who had difficulty identifying the current Queen. Restuss seemed even less interested in galactic dealings. The populace rarely discussed the raging civil war, but when they did, it was as if the conflict was taking place in some far distant corner of the galaxy.<ref name="AED" /> All that would change however, when by at least 1 ABY,<ref name="TERCexplain">According to ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'', ''[[Star Wars Galaxies: The Ruins of Dantooine]]'' took place in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]]. As the novel was written before [[2006]], and it is implied [[Restuss]] was still intact during this [[Time/Legends|time]], this article assumes that the [[Battle of Restuss]] began sometime during or after 1 ABY.</ref> the Galactic Empire started using a secret [[Research facility (Restuss)|research facility]] in the city of Restuss to develop an [[Energy cell/Legends|energy cell]] capable of powering a [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] scale installation. This power supply, known as the [[Star Core]], was devised by [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] Palpatine and was designed to be small enough to fit in the palm of a [[Limb/Legends|hand]].<ref name="CtAEmp">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=66904&resource=features|text=''Call to Arms, Fight for the Empire!''}}</ref> The Rebellion, eager to claim the Star Core for themselves, established a [[Rebel Base (Restuss)|base]] north of Restuss in preparation for a major assault on the city.<ref name="CtAReb">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=66905&resource=features|text=''Call to Arms, Aid the Rebellion!''}}</ref> The Empire responded by evacuating the city of its civilian population,<ref name="Ruins2">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=66906&resource=features|text=Ruins of Restuss}}</ref> and building up a [[Imperial Base (Restuss)|base]] of their own south of the city.<ref name="CtAEmp" /> In preparation for a large [[Battle of Restuss|battle]], both the Empire and Rebellion oversaw missions to other parts of the galaxy, eliminating ground forces, fighting for control in various [[Star system/Legends|star systems]], and [[Mining/Legends|mining]] for resources from [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]] in the [[Kessel system/Legends|Kessel system]] and deep space. After much preparation, both sides finally engaged in a full scale battle in the streets and skies over Restuss. During the climactic battle, the Star Core unexpectedly detonated, resulting in mass devastation to the city.<ref name="AED" /> Because the Star Core was only in the development stage, it did not reach its full destructive capacity. Otherwise, the blast would have potentially been powerful enough to destroy half the moon of Rori.<ref name="Ruins" /> With Restuss in ruins, the battle continued, but neither side achieved a clear and decisive victory. After the Star Core was destroyed, both sides struggled to maintain control over the ruins so that they could salvage the remains of the Imperial research project.<ref name="AED" /> The battle resulted in increased hostilities between Imperial and Rebel forces in other parts of the galaxy, including Naboo, [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], and [[Talus/Legends|Talus]],<ref name="GalaxyWar">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=66909&resource=features|text=''A Galaxy At War''}}</ref><ref name="AED" /> until at least [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].<ref name="SWGDate">According to its [[opening crawl]], ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'' was set sometime after [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. One character in the [[Star Wars video games|game]], [[Ruwan Tokai]], referenced the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|destruction]] of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] as occurring one [[Standard year/Legends|year]] earlier, placing the timeline somewhere around [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]]. However, the existence of other characters and quests in the game indicated a timeline of anywhere from [[0 ABY/Legends|0]] to [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], one moon can be seen in the skies of Naboo during at least a couple distant surface shots. However, Ohma-D'un is the only moon that appears clearly in any closeup shots,<ref name="Phantom">{{Film|I}}</ref> as later confirmed by its entry in the ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''.<ref name="Ohma">{{CSWECite|II|405|Ohma-D'un}}</ref>

Rori was first mentioned, albeit indirectly, in the [[2001]] paperback supplement to the [[Wizards of the Coast]] ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'', ''[[Secrets of Naboo]]''. Although it is not identified as Rori, the book confirms that Naboo had three moons.<ref name="Secrets">''[[Secrets of Naboo]]''</ref> In the ''[[HoloNet News Vol. 531 53]]'' regional article titled ''Naboo Miners Clog Ports in Protests'', the [[Naboo Moon Mining Union]] is credited with transforming "one of Naboo's smaller moons into a very lucrative [[kassoti]]-spice mining operation."<ref name="HoloNet">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|53|regional/13425_1.html|Naboo Miners Clog Ports in Protest}}</ref> As ''The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia'' identifies Ohma-Dun as Naboo's largest moon, this seemingly implies the possibility that Rori may be one of the two smaller moons involved.<ref name="Ohma" /> However, the ''The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia'' dispels this notion by further specifying that the Mining Union transformed the ''smallest'' moon of Naboo,<ref name="MoonUnion">{{CSWECite|II|353|Naboo Moon Mining Union}}</ref> which would have been the [[third moon of Naboo]], which ''[[Nexus of Power]]'' identified as the tiniest of the three moons.<ref name="NoP">''[[Nexus of Power]]''</ref> Nevertheless, the [[HoloNet News (original website)|HoloNet News]] article's usage of the plural "smaller moons" still constitutes an indirect mention of Rori.<ref name="HoloNet" /> Rori receives a similar indirect mention in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], when the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] Mace Windu refers to "spice miners on the moons of Naboo."<ref name="AotC" />

Rori was one of the ten original worlds included in the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'']], a [[Roleplaying game|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]] developed by [[Sony]] Online Entertainment and published by [[LucasArts]], prior to its closure on [[December 15]], [[2011]].<ref name="AED" /><ref name="Shutdown">{{SonyCite|url=playerinfo|text=IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ''STAR WARS'' GALAXIES™}}</ref> Although the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] [[Canon|continuity]] already established that Naboo had three moons, the ''Star Wars Galaxies'' team was responsible for naming and defining Rori. Including the moon allowed the team to reuse many of Naboo's creatures in another location, although the world artists did take great pains to distinguish Rori's terrain by incorporating mud flats and bogs.<ref name="Pixel">''[[From Pencil to Pixel: The Art of Star Wars Galaxies]]''</ref> In the game, Rori had the shortest rotation period of only 30 [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]]. However, this was purely game mechanics. For example, the game set the rotation periods of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], Naboo and Corellia at 3 hours,<ref name="Hints">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=68086&month=112008|text=Friday Feature &ndash; The Best of Tips and Hints}}</ref> despite actually being 23, 26 and 25 hours respectively.<ref name="TEA" />
